hints: Divide term by term to obtain $\frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} - \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = 1 - \tan^2\theta$.
walkthrough:
Express the numerator and denominator in terms of $\cos^2\theta$ using $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{1 - 2\sin^2\theta}{1 - \sin^2\theta} = \frac{(1 - \sin^2\theta) - \sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$$

Split into two fractions and simplify to reach the RHS:
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} - \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta} = 1 - \tan^2\theta$$

Substitute the identity into the given equation:
$$1 - \tan^2\theta = 2\tan^4\theta \implies 2\tan^4\theta + \tan^2\theta - 1 = 0$$

Solve for the valid roots (noting $\tan^2\theta + 1 > 0$ for all real $\theta$):
$$2\tan^2\theta = 1 \implies \tan^2\theta = 0.5 \implies \tan\theta = \pm\sqrt{0.5} \approx \pm 0.7071$$

Find both solutions in the interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 180^\circ$:
$$\text{For } \tan\theta = \sqrt{0.5}: \quad \theta = \tan^{-1}(0.7071) \approx 35.3^\circ$$
$$\text{For } \tan\theta = -\sqrt{0.5}: \quad \theta = 180^\circ - 35.3^\circ = 144.7^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 35.3^\circ, \quad 144.7^\circ)$$
